name: Vertical Rectus Abdominis Myocutaneous (VRAM) Flap

dominant_pedicle.artery: Deep inferior epigastric artery (pelvis/groin) or Superior epigastric artery (sternum)
dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: External iliac artery (DIEA) or Internal mammary artery (SEA)

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Superior reliability vs TRAM because entire paddle overlies rectus perforators.

nerves.donor_numbness_note: Anterior abdominal sensory loss along vertical scar.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Generous obliterative bulk for pelvic exenteration dead space.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Inferior DIEA origin (pelvis/groin) or costal margin (sternum)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Gold standard pedicled flap for APR/pelvic exenteration, perineum, groin, and lower sternum.

indications: Pelvic dead space obliteration & perineal reconstruction after APR/exenteration
Groin oncologic / exposed femoral graft coverage
Lower sternal wounds
contraindications: Bilateral ostomies through both rectus muscles
Prior division of DIEA/IMA
advantages: Exceptionally reliable in heavily irradiated pelvic beds
Harvested through existing laparotomy
disadvantages: Abdominal wall hernia/bulge risk
Vertical abdominal scar

donor_site.closure: Preserve anterior sheath below arcuate line; primary ± mesh closure.

preoperative_planning: Coordinate contralateral ostomy siting
Review staging CT for DIEA patency
technique.design: Vertical ellipse over non-ostomy rectus abdominis.
harvest_steps: 1. Leave 1–2 cm medial/lateral fascial cuffs and keep sheath below arcuate line intact.
2. Divide superior epigastric pedicle and elevate rectus off posterior sheath.
3. Mobilize DIEA pedicle and pass intraperitoneally into pelvis without twist.
4. Reinforce abdominal wall closure.
pearls: Keep anterior rectus fascia intact below the arcuate line.
pitfalls: Twisting the DIEA pedicle during pelvic delivery.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Medial Sural Artery Perforator (MSAP) Flap

perforators.label: Main MSAP Cluster
perforators.location: 8–12 cm distal to popliteal crease midpoint toward medial malleolus

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Paired venae comitantes; optional greater saphenous vein backup.

motor: Tibial motor branch to medial gastrocnemius — preserve

dimensions.thickness_notes: Consistently thin and pliable — strong alternative to RFFF without sacrificing a major artery.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Pedicled to knee/proximal tibia sparing gastrocnemius; free flap for oral cavity, hand, and foot.

indications: Oral cavity / tongue reconstruction (thin alternative to RFFF)
Hand, foot, and distal ankle thin coverage
Pedicled knee resurfacing
contraindications: Severe popliteal PVD
Very large defects (>15 × 8 cm)
advantages: Thin pliable skin without sacrificing radial artery
Preserves gastrocnemius muscle
Long pedicle (8–14 cm)
disadvantages: Tedious intramuscular dissection
Donor STSG if width >6 cm

donor_site.closure: Primary if ≤5–6 cm; STSG if wider.

preoperative_planning: Draw popliteal crease midpoint to medial malleolus line
Doppler 8–12 cm distal
technique.design: Center ellipse over strongest Doppler perforators 8–12 cm distal to crease.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise anterior margin to identify perforators.
2. Split medial gastrocnemius fibers carefully to medial sural trunk.
3. Preserve tibial motor nerve.
4. Complete posterior incision and divide pedicle.
pearls: Seamlessly converts to medial gastrocnemius flap if no usable perforator is found.
pitfalls: Small muscular side-branch oozing after tourniquet release.

references.book: Blondeel PN et al. Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Soleus / Hemisoleus Muscle Flap

classification.mathes_nahai: Type II (proximal dominant + distal segmental minor pedicles)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Proximal muscular branches of posterior tibial and peroneal arteries

minor_pedicles: Distal segmental branches of posterior tibial artery
vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Preserving lateral half (hemisoleus) maintains ankle plantarflexion.
vascular_variants: Proximally based hemisoleus is far more reliable than distally based

dimensions.thickness_notes: Muscle belly surfaced with meshed STSG.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Workhorse regional muscle flap for middle third of tibia.

indications: Middle-third tibial open fractures / exposed bone or hardware (outside severe crush zone)
contraindications: High-energy posterior compartment crush injury
Distal-third tibial/ankle defects
advantages: Reliable pedicled middle-third tibial coverage without microsurgery
disadvantages: Often within zone of injury in high-energy trauma
High tip necrosis rate if distally based

donor_site.closure: Primary medial calf closure; STSG over transposed muscle.
morbidity: Mild plantarflexion weakness if full soleus used

preoperative_planning: Verify posterior tibial perfusion and muscle viability outside crush zone
technique.design: Longitudinal medial leg incision 2 cm posterior to tibia.
harvest_steps: 1. Separate soleus from gastrocnemius and deep posterior compartment (protect PT bundle).
2. Split soleus longitudinally along midline raphe.
3. Divide distal minor pedicles confirming brisk distal muscle bleeding.
4. Transpose over middle third tibia and apply STSG.
pearls: Always visualize and safeguard the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle immediately deep to soleus.
pitfalls: Attempting distally based soleus for large distal-third ankle defects.

recipient_vessels_options: Pedicled on proximal posterior tibial branches

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Transverse Upper Gracilis (TUG) Flap

dominant_pedicle.artery: Ascending branch of medial circumflex femoral artery (MCFA)

perforators.label: Proximal Gracilis Perforators
perforators.location: 6–10 cm below groin crease over proximal gracilis

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Preserve greater saphenous vein anteriorly to protect lymphatics.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Transferred as a free flap to internal mammary vessels.

indications: Small-to-moderate autologous breast reconstruction when abdomen unavailable
contraindications: Large breast volume requirement (unless stacked)
Lower-extremity lymphedema
advantages: Consistent harvest without perforator dissection
Two-team supine frog-leg harvest
disadvantages: Sacrifices gracilis muscle
Short pedicle and groin dehiscence/lymphedema risk

preoperative_planning: Mark groin crease and adductor longus standing
technique.design: Transverse crescent ≤7–8 cm wide centered over proximal gracilis.
harvest_steps: 1. Preserve GSV and anterior femoral triangle lymphatics.
2. Retract adductor longus and dissect MCFA to profunda.
3. Divide muscle distally/proximally and cone skin crescent into breast mound.
pearls: Stop anterior incision at anterior border of adductor longus.
pitfalls: Over-resecting vertical height causing labial spreading.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Posterior Interosseous Artery (PIA) Flap

classification.cormack_lamberty: Type C (septum between ECU and EDM)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Posterior interosseous artery (retrograde via distal AIA arcade)

minor_pedicles: Distal anastomosis with anterior interosseous artery 2 cm proximal to DRUJ

perforators.label: ECU–EDM Septal Perforators
perforators.location: Midpoint of lateral epicondyle–ulnar head line
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Pivot point 2 cm proximal to DRUJ

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Keep a fascial/subcutaneous cuff and open skin bridge to prevent venous congestion.
vascular_variants: Absent distal AIA–PIA communication in ~5% — verify before dividing proximal PIA

dimensions.thickness_notes: Thin dorsal forearm skin matching dorsal hand texture.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Reaches dorsal hand, first webspace, and volar wrist while sparing radial and ulnar arteries.

indications: Dorsal hand defects with exposed extensor tendons
First webspace contracture release
contraindications: Prior dorsal wrist trauma disrupting AIA–PIA arcade
advantages: Spares radial and ulnar arteries
Single-stage regional transfer
disadvantages: Delicate dissection near PIN
Venous congestion risk

preoperative_planning: Draw lateral epicondyle–ulnar head line
Doppler mid-forearm perforators
technique.design: Racquet-shaped skin extension over pedicle to eliminate tight wrist tunneling.
harvest_steps: 1. Confirm intact distal AIA–PIA arcade first.
2. Safeguard ECU–EDM septocutaneous perforators.
3. Carefully separate PIN proximally and verify retrograde flow before ligating proximal PIA.
4. Rotate into dorsal hand without tension.
pearls: Use a teardrop skin tail over the pedicle instead of a tight tunnel.
pitfalls: Injuring PIN proximally causing finger drop.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Lateral Arm Free Flap (PRCA)

minor_pedicles: Distal elbow recurrent arcade (reverse lateral arm for elbow)

perforators.label: Lateral Intermuscular Septum
perforators.location: Line from deltoid insertion to lateral epicondyle
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Between triceps posteriorly and brachialis/brachioradialis anteriorly

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Paired venae comitantes; radial nerve lies directly adjacent in spiral groove.
vascular_variants: Small arterial caliber (1.2–1.8 mm) requires meticulous microsurgery

motor: Radial nerve in spiral groove — PROTECT carefully
sensory: Lower lateral cutaneous nerve of arm / posterior cutaneous nerve of forearm

dimensions.thickness_notes: Thinner distally when extended over lateral epicondyle onto proximal forearm.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Free transfer (or elbow for reverse pedicled)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Same-limb free transfer for hand/wrist defects; oral cavity/parotid contour.

indications: Same-extremity free flap for dorsal/volar hand defects
Oral cavity / facial contour defects
Reverse pedicled elbow coverage
contraindications: Obesity causing excessive upper arm thickness
advantages: Spares major hand arteries
Single-limb surgery under regional block possible
Primary closure up to 6–7 cm
disadvantages: Smaller arterial caliber & shorter pedicle than RFFF
Risk of radial nerve neuropraxia

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with arm across chest or on hand table.
preoperative_planning: Draw deltoid insertion to lateral epicondyle line
technique.design: Fusiform ellipse centered along deltoid–lateral epicondyle axis (extend distally for thinner skin).
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate posteriorly over triceps fascia to lateral septum.
2. Elevate anteriorly over brachioradialis/brachialis.
3. Identify and protect radial nerve in spiral groove while tracing PRCA proximally.
4. Divide pedicle and close donor arm primarily.
pearls: Extending the paddle 4–6 cm distal to the lateral epicondyle yields markedly thinner tissue for hand resurfacing.
pitfalls: Excessive traction on the radial nerve in the spiral groove.

name: Scapular / Parascapular Flap
tissue_components: Lateral scapular border / scapular tip bone (optional chimeric)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Circumflex scapular artery (transverse = scapular; descending = parascapular)
dominant_pedicle.veins: Paired venae comitantes joining subscapular vein

minor_pedicles: Angular branch of thoracodorsal artery (for scapular tip bone)

perforators.label: Triangular Space Exit
perforators.location: Bounded by teres minor (superior), teres major (inferior), long head of triceps (lateral)

vascular_variants: Rarely affected by peripheral arterial disease — ideal backup when fibula is contraindicated

dimensions.thickness_notes: Thick, durable, hairless skin; can be combined chimerically with LD muscle and 10–14 cm lateral scapular bone.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Free transfer to mandible, midface/maxilla (scapular tip), scalp, or extremity; pedicled to axilla/shoulder.

indications: Complex multi-component head & neck composite defects (chimeric skin + muscle + bone)
Alternative osteocutaneous mandibular/maxillary reconstruction when fibula is contraindicated (PVD)
Axillary burn contracture
contraindications: Need for >14 cm vascularized bone segment
Two-team harvest is difficult due to lateral decubitus position
advantages: Spared from atherosclerosis
Unmatched chimeric subscapular versatility with independent skin/bone mobility
disadvantages: Requires lateral decubitus positioning
Shorter/thinner bone than fibula; widened back scar

morbidity: Temporary shoulder stiffness if bone harvested

preoperative_planning: Palpate triangular space along lateral scapular border
Handheld Doppler
technique.design: Horizontal (scapular) or vertical/oblique (parascapular) ellipse anchored over triangular space.
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate suprafascially from distal toward triangular space.
2. Identify transverse and descending cutaneous branches emerging from triangular space.
3. Trace circumflex scapular vessels deep between teres minor and major to subscapular trunk.
4. Include lateral scapular border bone via periosteal branches if needed.
pearls: Ideal backup osteocutaneous flap in elderly patients with severe tibial peripheral vascular disease.
pitfalls: Widened donor scar if closed under tension across mobile shoulder.

name: Deep Circumflex Iliac Artery (DCIA) Osteocutaneous Flap
tissue_components: Curved iliac crest bone (up to 14–16 cm)

dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: External iliac artery just above inguinal ligament
dominant_pedicle.veins: Paired venae comitantes uniting into single DCIV crossing external iliac artery

minor_pedicles: Ascending branch of DCIA (supplies internal oblique muscle)

perforators.label: Iliac Crest Musculocutaneous Row
perforators.location: 2–3 cm medial to iliac crest posterior to ASIS
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Must preserve a 2-cm cuff of abdominal wall muscles if skin paddle included

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Single large DCIV drains to external iliac vein.
vascular_variants: Ascending branch arises ~1 cm medial to ASIS

sensory: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (crosses near ASIS — protect)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Natural curvature & tall alveolar height ideal for hemimandibular reconstruction and dental implants.

indications: Hemimandibular osseous defects requiring tall alveolar height for dental implants
Alternative to fibula in severe lower-limb PVD
contraindications: Prior inguinal/iliac hernia mesh repair
Need for >16 cm bone length
advantages: Natural mandibular curvature and tall vertical bone stock
Internal oblique muscle provides thin mucosalizing intraoral lining
disadvantages: Donor abdominal hernia risk (careful 3-layer repair needed)
Bulky skin paddle; shorter pedicle than fibula

donor_site.closure: Meticulous layered reattachment of transversalis/internal/external oblique to residual iliac bone ± mesh.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with sandbag under ipsilateral hip.
preoperative_planning: CTA of external iliac/DCIA
VSP templates
technique.design: Incision 2 cm superior to inguinal ligament extending along iliac crest.
harvest_steps: 1. Expose external iliac vessels above inguinal ligament and trace DCIA laterally.
2. Identify ascending branch entering internal oblique.
3. Harvest desired iliac crest bone segment preserving medial periosteum.
4. Perform meticulous multilayer abdominal wall closure.
pearls: Use internal oblique muscle (which mucosalizes cleanly) instead of a bulky skin paddle for oral lining.
pitfalls: Inadequate abdominal wall closure leading to lateral flank hernia.

name: Temporoparietal Fascia Flap (TPFF)
tissue_components: Ultra-thin vascularized temporoparietal fascia (± calvarial bone or STSG)

perforators.label: STA Preauricular Entry
perforators.location: Directly anterior to tragus crossing posterior root of zygoma
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Courses directly within TPFF (continuous with SMAS and galea)

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Superficial temporal vein lies just posterior to artery.
vascular_variants: Variable bifurcation level above zygomatic arch

motor: Frontal branch of facial nerve (courses along Pitanguy line deep to/within anterior TPFF — PROTECT!)

dimensions.thickness_notes: 2–4 mm ultra-thin gliding fascia; ideal for ear reconstruction frameworks and dorsal hand/finger tendons.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Pedicled to ear, orbit, midface, lateral skull base, and eyebrow; free flap for ultra-thin hand/tendon gliding.

indications: Ear reconstruction (microtia / trauma framework coverage + STSG)
Orbital/skull base lining
Free ultra-thin gliding coverage over dorsal hand/foot tendons
contraindications: Prior ipsilateral external carotid or STA ligation
advantages: Thinnest pliable vascularized fascia in the body (2–4 mm)
Hidden hairline scar
disadvantages: Risk of scalp alopecia if dissected too close to hair follicles
Risk of frontal branch facial nerve injury

preoperative_planning: Map STA frontal and parietal branches with Doppler
Mark Pitanguy line (0.5 cm below tragus to 1.5 cm above lateral brow)
technique.design: Vertical T or zigzag temporal scalp incision.
harvest_steps: 1. Dissect immediately deep to hair follicles (avoid follicle injury) to expose TPFF.
2. Elevate TPFF off deep temporal fascia in loose areolar plane.
3. Stay posterior to frontal branch of facial nerve anteriorly.
4. Transpose onto ear/orbit or divide STA/STV for free transfer.
pearls: Keep dissection directly beneath hair bulbs to prevent alopecia while keeping STA intact inside the fascia.
pitfalls: Injuring the frontal branch of CN VII crossing the mid-zygomatic arch.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Distally Based Reverse Sural Neurocutaneous Flap

classification.perforator_type: Septocutaneous peroneal perforator anastomosis (~5 cm above lateral malleolus)

tissue_components: Sural nerve & lesser saphenous vein (vasa nervorum/vasorum)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Median superficial sural artery (retrograde via peroneal septocutaneous perforator ~5 cm proximal to lateral malleolus)
dominant_pedicle.veins: Lesser saphenous vein and accompanying venules

perforators.label: Distal Peroneal Pivot Perforator
perforators.location: 5 cm proximal to lateral malleolus along posterior fibular border
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: NEVER dissect closer than 5 cm above lateral malleolus

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Prone to venous congestion — preserve a 3–4 cm wide adipofascial pedicle and avoid subcutaneous tunneling (open skin bridge or skin-graft pedicle).
vascular_variants: High complication rate in severe PVD, diabetes, venous stasis, or elderly smokers

sensory: Sural nerve (sacrificed — causes permanent lateral foot numbness)
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Permanent lateral border of foot numbness.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Useful non-microsurgical option for small-to-moderate Achilles, heel, and malleolar defects.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Reaches Achilles tendon, posterior heel, lateral/medial malleoli, and distal anterior ankle.

indications: Small-to-moderate distal tibia, Achilles, heel, or malleolar defects when free flap is contraindicated
contraindications: Severe PVD / peroneal artery occlusion
Severe venous insufficiency
Zone of injury involving distal lateral leg
advantages: Avoids microsurgery and spares major tibial/peroneal arteries
Rapid harvest
disadvantages: High rate of venous congestion & partial tip necrosis (15–30%)
Sacrifices sural nerve (lateral foot numbness)

donor_site.closure: Primary if ≤4–5 cm; STSG if wider.
donor_site.functional_loss: Sensory loss along lateral foot border.

preoperative_planning: Doppler peroneal perforator 5 cm proximal to lateral malleolus
Consider 10–14 day surgical delay in high-risk patients
technique.design: Paddle centered on midline posterior calf (middle third); 3–4 cm wide adipofascial pedicle extending to 5 cm above lateral malleolus.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise proximal paddle, divide and include sural nerve and lesser saphenous vein cleanly.
2. Elevate subfascially keeping a 3–4 cm adipofascial pedicle.
3. Stop dissection strictly 5 cm above lateral malleolus.
4. Rotate to heel/ankle over an incised open skin bridge (do not tunnel tightly) and skin-graft pedicle.
pearls: Never tunnel a reverse sural pedicle under tight ankle skin; incise the bridge and apply STSG over the pedicle.
pitfalls: Dissecting distal to the 5-cm pivot point and dividing the peroneal anastomotic perforator.

recipient_vessels_options: Pedicled retrograde via distal peroneal perforator

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Peroneal Artery Perforator Propeller Flap

perforators.label: Distal Peroneal Septal Perforator
perforators.location: 5–15 cm proximal to lateral malleolus along posterior fibular border

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Skeletonize perforator cleanly for ≥2 cm to allow gentle twist up to 180° without venous kinking.
vascular_variants: Check both clockwise and counterclockwise rotation directions intraoperatively

nerves.donor_numbness_note: Preserves sural nerve unlike reverse sural flap.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Like-with-like thin lateral ankle coverage without microsurgery.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Selected peroneal perforator adjacent to defect
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Propeller rotation up to 180° into distal tibia, lateral malleolus, or Achilles defect.

indications: Small-to-moderate distal leg, Achilles, or lateral malleolus defects with healthy adjacent tissue
contraindications: Perforator inside high-energy zone of injury
Severe PVD
advantages: Like-with-like thin resurfacing
Spares sural nerve and major arteries; no microsurgery
disadvantages: Venous congestion if perforator insufficiently skeletonized
Limited to small/moderate defects

donor_site.closure: Primary or small STSG on proximal secondary defect.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with hip bump or lateral.
preoperative_planning: Handheld Doppler along posterior fibular border adjacent to defect
technique.design: Make exploratory incision first, locate best perforator, then finalize propeller blade lengths (large blade ≥ distance from perforator to far defect edge + 1–2 cm).
harvest_steps: 1. Explore anteriorly to visualize septocutaneous perforator.
2. Free all fascial strands around perforator for 2–3 cm.
3. Test clockwise vs counterclockwise rotation and select direction with least twist.
4. Inset tension-free and monitor capillary refill.
pearls: Always rotate in the direction (clockwise vs counterclockwise) that creates less pedicle torsion.
pitfalls: Leaving a constricting fascial band around the perforator during 180° twist.

references.book: Blondeel PN et al. Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Gluteus Maximus Rotation / V-Y Advancement Flap

classification.mathes_nahai: Type III (superior and inferior gluteal arteries)

tissue_components: Gluteus maximus muscle (optional; spare in ambulatory patients)

perforators.label: SGA/IGA Perforator Zone
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Large arc allows re-advancement if recurrence occurs

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Extremely robust dual vascularity (Mathes–Nahai Type III).
vascular_variants: Design large rotation arc so flap can be re-rotated for recurrent pressure sores

motor: Inferior gluteal nerve (preserve in ambulatory patients)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Durable padded tissue ideal for sacral and ischial pressure sores.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Inferolateral gluteal base (rotation) or perforator base (V-Y)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Covers midline sacral and ischial pressure injuries.

indications: Stage IV sacral pressure injuries (unilateral or bilateral V-Y / rotation)
Ischial pressure injuries (inferior gluteal)
contraindications: Uncontrolled osteomyelitis, malnutrition (prealbumin low), or unaddressed spasticity/offloading
advantages: Large rotation arc can be re-advanced if ulcer recurs
Durable padding over bony prominence
disadvantages: High recurrence rate without strict postoperative pressure offloading
Avoid muscle sacrifice in ambulatory patients

donor_site.closure: Primary tension-free closure over closed-suction drains.
donor_site.functional_loss: None when muscle preserved in ambulatory patients.

preoperative_planning: Optimize nutrition and control spasticity
Excise bursa and shave bony prominence cleanly
technique.design: Generous superiorly based rotation arc (or bilateral V-Y triangles) avoiding scars over weight-bearing ischium.
harvest_steps: 1. Excise pseudo-bursa completely and perform sacral ostectomy.
2. Elevate fasciocutaneous (ambulatory) or myocutaneous (paraplegic) flap.
3. Mobilize tension-free into defect and suture deep dermis securely over drains.
4. Maintain strict air-fluidized mattress offloading for 3–6 weeks.
pearls: Always design flaps large enough to be re-rotated if the patient develops a recurrence years later.
pitfalls: Closing under tension or failing to shave underlying bony prominence.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Medial Plantar Artery (Instep) Flap
tissue_components: Cutaneous branches of medial plantar nerve (sensate!)

perforators.label: Instep Septal Perforators
perforators.location: Non-weight-bearing medial instep between abductor hallucis and FDB

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Accompanying venae comitantes + optional saphenous vein.
vascular_variants: Verify patent dorsalis pedis / lateral plantar artery before harvest

motor: Protect main medial plantar nerve motor trunk
sensory: Cutaneous fascicles of medial plantar nerve (interfascicular dissection)
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Avoid injury to digital sensory fascicles to toes.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Unique glabrous, vertically septated, sensate plantar skin — gold standard for weight-bearing heel.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Pedicled directly to weight-bearing plantar heel; free flap for palmar hand or contralateral heel.

indications: Weight-bearing plantar heel defects (gold standard 'like-with-like' sensate glabrous reconstruction)
Free glabrous palmar hand/digit resurfacing
contraindications: Posterior tibial artery occlusion or severe diabetic peripheral neuropathy/PVD
advantages: True glabrous, shear-resistant, sensate 'like-with-like' tissue for heel
disadvantages: Donor instep requires STSG
Limited size (<10 × 7 cm)

preoperative_planning: Verify posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis pulses/Doppler
technique.design: Template within non-weight-bearing medial arch strictly proximal to metatarsal heads.
harvest_steps: 1. Expose medial plantar vessels between abductor hallucis and FDB.
2. Include plantar fascia with skin paddle and preserve cutaneous sensory fascicles via interfascicular neurolysis.
3. Transpose proximally to weight-bearing heel and skin-graft donor instep.
pearls: Keep donor harvest strictly within the non-weight-bearing instep arch.
pitfalls: Dividing main medial plantar nerve causing plantar toe numbness.

complications: Sensory neuropathy if main nerve injured

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Nasolabial Flap (Superiorly / Inferiorly Based)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Angular / facial artery perforators and subdermal plexus

perforators.label: Nasolabial Perforator Zone
perforators.location: Lateral to alar base along melolabial crease
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Concealed donor scar within natural melolabial fold

vascular_variants: May be designed as 1-stage transposition or 2-stage interpolated flap to preserve alar-facial sulcus

motor: Buccal facial nerve branches lie deep — stay subcutaneous

dimensions.thickness_notes: Tendency to contract into a rounded contour — ideal for convex nasal ala.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Superior alar base or inferior oral commissure
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Reaches nasal ala, nasal floor, upper/lower lip, and anterior floor of mouth (inferiorly based).

indications: Isolated nasal alar subunit reconstruction (2-stage interpolated)
Upper lip and anterior oral cavity defects
contraindications: Transferring beard hair onto nasal ala in males without epilation plan
advantages: Donor scar hidden seamlessly in melolabial fold
Excellent color match and natural convex contour for ala
disadvantages: Can blunt alar-facial groove if 1-stage transposition is used
Pin-cushioning

donor_site.closure: Primary closure directly along nasolabial crease.

preoperative_planning: Draw template along melolabial fold
Decide 1-stage vs 2-stage interpolated (preferred for ala)
technique.design: Place medial incision directly in melolabial crease.
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate distally in subcutaneous plane leaving 2–3 mm fat; keep proximal subcutaneous pedicle intact.
2. Insert structural alar batten cartilage graft to prevent alar collapse.
3. Inset into alar subunit and close cheek crease primarily.
4. Divide interpolated pedicle at 3 weeks.
pearls: A 2-stage interpolated melolabial flap preserves the crisp alar-facial sulcus far better than a 1-stage transposition.
pitfalls: Omitting a cartilage batten graft, leading to nasal valve collapse.

name: Z-Plasty & Local Transposition / Rhomboid (Limberg) Techniques
region: Universal (any body region with adjacent laxity)

classification.perforator_type: Subdermal plexus (or fascial perforators for Keystone)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Random-pattern dermal and subdermal vascular plexus

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Respect safe length-to-width ratios (~3:1 on face, ~1.5:1 on trunk/extremities) and avoid acute tip angles (<30°) that compromise tip perfusion.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Provides exact local color, thickness, and hair-bearing match.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Lengthens scar contractures, reorients scars into relaxed skin tension lines (RSTLs), and closes small-to-moderate cutaneous defects.

indications: Linear burn or scar contracture release (Z-plasty)
Small-to-moderate cutaneous oncology defects (Limberg rhomboid, Bilobed on nasal tip <1.5 cm, Keystone on trunk/extremities)
Reorienting scars parallel to RSTLs
contraindications: Insufficient adjacent skin laxity perpendicular to tension vector
Heavily irradiated or scarred surrounding skin
advantages: Exact color and texture match ('like-with-like')
Single-stage, rapid, low morbidity
disadvantages: Adds scar length; limited by adjacent tissue laxity

donor_site.closure: Primary tension-free closure along lines of maximal extensibility (LME).
donor_site.functional_loss: None; improves joint/webspace mobility when releasing contractures.

preoperative_planning: Identify RSTLs and lines of maximal extensibility (LME) via pinch test
Use Z-Plasty Simulator to verify angle and gain
landmarks: Limberg 60°/120° rhombus with short diagonal parallel to LME
technique.design: For classic Z-plasty: equal-length central and lateral limbs at 60° (central limb rotates 90° upon transposition, lengthening by 75%).
harvest_steps: 1. Mark equal limb lengths carefully with caliper.
2. Incise and undermine in appropriate subcutaneous plane.
3. Transpose triangular flaps gently using skin hooks (never crush tips with forceps).
4. Place half-buried horizontal mattress (Gillies corner) sutures at tips.
pearls: Use the 60° Z-plasty as the clinical sweet spot (75% theoretical gain without excessive transverse tension).
pitfalls: Crushing acute flap tips with toothed forceps causing tip epidermolysis.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: First Dorsal Metacarpal Artery (Kite / Foucher) Flap

dominant_pedicle.artery: First dorsal metacarpal artery (ulnar/radial branch to index)
dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: Radial artery at apex of first intermetacarpal space
dominant_pedicle.veins: Dorsal cutaneous veins & venae comitantes within adipofascial pedicle

perforators.label: FDMA Origin (Snuffbox Apex)
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Include fascia of first dorsal interosseous muscle with pedicle

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Preserve dorsal subcutaneous veins in a 1-cm adipofascial pedicle.
vascular_variants: Superficial (fascial) course in ~57%, subfascial/intramuscular in ~43% — always include FDI fascia

sensory: Dorsal branch of superficial radial nerve (provides sensate thumb reconstruction)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Thin, pliable sensate resurfacing for dorsal or volar thumb defects.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Apex of first webspace (between 1st & 2nd metacarpal bases)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Reaches dorsal and volar thumb pulp, IP joint, and first webspace.

indications: Volar thumb pulp defects (>1.5 cm, beyond Moberg reach) needing sensate coverage
Dorsal thumb defects with exposed EPL tendon or IP joint
contraindications: Severe crush injury to first webspace or radial snuffbox
advantages: Single-stage sensate thumb resurfacing without microsurgery
Reliable anatomy when FDI fascia is included
disadvantages: Donor dorsal index requires FTSG
Cortical reorientation needed initially (patient feels touch on index)

donor_site.closure: Full-thickness skin graft over intact extensor paratenon on dorsal proximal phalanx of index.
morbidity: Mild PIP stiffness if paratenon stripped

technique.patient_positioning: Supine, arm on hand table under tourniquet.
preoperative_planning: Doppler FDMA over first dorsal interosseous muscle
technique.design: Island over dorsal proximal phalanx of index strictly between MCP and PIP joints.
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate skin island over index proximal phalanx strictly preserving extensor paratenon.
2. Raise 1-cm wide adipofascial pedicle including dorsal veins, radial nerve branch, and FDI muscle fascia back to webspace apex.
3. Pass gently through wide subcutaneous tunnel (or open incision) to thumb defect.
4. Apply FTSG to dorsal index donor site.
pearls: Always include the fascia of the first dorsal interosseous muscle to avoid missing a subfascial FDMA.
pitfalls: Violating extensor paratenon on the index finger causing FTSG failure and stiffness.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications
